newsitem.title: Nigeria: Nigeria frees French pilot unconditionally.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria frees French pilot unconditionally.

text.p: Nigeria has freed a French pilot detained since June after he made an emergency landing near an area disputed by Nigeria and Cameroon.
A French embassy official in Lagos said on Wednesday Laurent Klinka was freed unconditionally.
"There are no conditions. They examined the case and they freed him," the official said, adding: "He is in good health."
Klinka, released after a plea by French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette, was staying in the French ambassador's residence in Lagos and would fly back to Paris on Saturday, a French statement said.
"We are pleased by the happy ending to this affair," the statement said. "We thank the Nigerian authorities and all those who intervened."

Klinka made an emergency landing in June at Nigeria's Calabar airport near the Bakassi peninsula, an oil-rich area disputed by Nigeria and Cameroon. He had been on a flight in a crop-spraying plane from Ivory Coast to Cameroon.
Lagos has accused France of siding with Cameroon, a former colony, in the dispute.
